# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **The ONLY cluster** — every failure | ALL 50 val tasks (8 "controllable" + 42 "infra"; the split is spurious) | Bind-mount ROOT `/mnt/data` (= `$SPREADSHEETBENCH_DATA_DIR`) is mode **0700** owned by uid 1004; the executor container runs as uid **1000**, so it cannot traverse the root → cannot read inputs (already 0644/0755) or write outputs (already 0777). `PermissionError`, output never written, reward 0.000. | CAPABILITY-GAP (environment/runner), NOT knowledge/behavioral | Runner code fix: make the mount root traversable |

There is **no spreadsheet-correctness signal anywhere** — every rollout died at the permission wall before any grading. The seed's generated code was correct on inspection (e.g. 30709 produced a valid date-extraction solution round 1). So there is no prompt cluster to target; a prompt edit here would be speculative and fails the REAL/VERIFIED tests.

## Changes made this iteration
| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | in-body guard (permission normalization) | `adapter.py::run_target` (BOTH the template `«redacted».py` and the runtime copy `.capevolve/project/adapters/adapter.py`) | After `host_out_dir` is computed, a guarded chmod ORs `0o055` (o+rx) onto `data_dir` when it lacks it: `cur=os.stat(data_dir).st_mode&0o777; if cur&0o055!=0o055: os.chmod(data_dir, cur|0o055)`, wrapped in try/except OSError. Generalizes to ANY dataset root created without world-traverse by any uid — the existing code already widens the output subtree the same way but forgot the root. | Yes — see blast radius below |

`prompt.md`: **left unchanged** (identical to champion/seed). It is already correct, and the only prior prompt edit (cand_0001) was REJECTED with broke={}. Adding more prose would be a speculative edit that fails the THREE TESTS.

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change)
- **adapter guard, failing state:** real data dir was `drwx------ 0700`. Guard `0o700 & 0o055 = 0 != 0o055` → TRUE → chmod to `0o755`. Confirmed: `before 0o700 → after 0o755`.
- **End-to-end (the real proof):** `docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 --user 1000:1000 -v <datadir>:/mnt/data python:3.11` — READ `/mnt/data/spreadsheet/30709/1_30709_input.xlsx` → `b'PK\x03\x04'` (valid xlsx); WROTE `/mnt/data/outputs/probe/x.txt` → `WROTE_OK`. Both raised `PermissionError` before the fix (root 0700). This is exactly the container the sandbox runs.
- **Blast radius (SAFE):** BOUNDED. (1) **Zero currently-passing tasks** (all 50 at 0.0), so no task's behavior can regress. (2) The guard fires ONLY when the root lacks o+rx (the exact violating condition); on an already-healthy 0755 root it is a no-op. (3) It only ADDS traverse/read on the root dir; input files stay 0644 (read-only to the uid-1000 container — verified they remain 0644), outputs stay 0777. It cannot make a working task fail. (4) `os` already imported; guarded by try/except so a non-owned dir is a best-effort no-op (real error still surfaces, as before).
- **Regression test:** `pytest core/tests/test_spreadsheetbench_recalc_perms.py` → **7 passed**.

## Process & features used
- Serial (no subagents): one uniform root cause across all 50 traces — fan-out would add no coverage. Diagnosed by reading the 30709 full trace (PermissionError on input read, then ~30 rounds of failed chmod/sudo/setpriv/namei probing) and confirming the identical `err`/feedback across all 50 score records.
- Prior iterations read: `./prior_iterations/cand_0001` (PROCESS) + JOURNAL + LEDGER RESULT. cand_0001 correctly diagnosed the mount bug but could only edit the prompt → REJECTED, val 0.000, broke={}. I did NOT re-add its env-error prompt rule (proven not to move the score). I acted on its explicit handover: "the correct action is to FIX THE RUNNER MOUNT PERMISSIONS."

## Good things to PRESERVE
- The `data_dir` root-traversal chmod in `run_target` — without it the whole benchmark is stuck at 0.000. Do not remove it or narrow the `0o055` widening.
- Keep `prompt.md` as-is until real spreadsheet-correctness clusters appear in healthy-env traces.

## Deliberately skipped
- All "spreadsheet-correctness" / prompt levers: no correctness signal exists yet (every failure was the permission wall). Revisit only after re-score confirms the env is healthy and genuine partial-credit/omission clusters appear.
- The 42 "infra" tasks were NOT skipped-as-unfixable — they share the SAME root cause as the 8 and are fixed by the same change.
